description.narrative: The objective of the strategy is to destabilise these structures by ensuring new women leaders are represented in policy and decision making spaces as well in convenings and conversations.

The program strategy aims to capacitate new women leaders, including WWDs and young women, on feminist leadership to build inclusive movements and alliances. The program recognises power structures, both visible and hidden, that exist within movements.

sector.narrative: Support for feminist, women-led and women's rights organisations and movements, and institutions (governmental and non-govermental) at all levels to enhance their effectiveness, influence and substainability (activities and core-funding). These organisations exist to bring about transformative change for gender equality and/or the rights of women and girls in developing countries. Their activities include agenda-setting, advocacy, policy dialogue, capacity development, awareness raising and prevention, service provision, conflict-prevention and peacebuilding, research, organising, and alliance and network building

For the year 2025, the consortium partner had submitted to MOFA a revised target of 0 in place of 10, based on the activity plan. Thus there was no target for this indicator.

The partner organized a Data Storytelling Workshop which was for 3 hour virtual session delved into the basic principles of data storytelling and data visualisation. It aimed to give those new to the craft an overview of its elements and some insights into key considerations in the creative process and particularly how to use data storytelling in strategic and creative communications around GBV to different stakeholders. 35 participants from 5 countries took part in the session.

The partner organized an online workshop on Understanding Anti-Carceral Feminism which was attended by 20 participants. The workshop increased participants' capacity and knowledge around the history of the carceral state and feminism, and what intersectionality looks like in the context of anti-carceral work.

Young Women & Women with Disabilities participating in political processes

IWRAW AP in partnership with CREA co-hosted a side event at the Global Disability Summit–‘Dismantling ableism in sexual and reproductive health and rights: What kinds of cross-movement cooperation and transformational leadership do we need?’. As a participatory reflection circle, it brought together 50 activists from the Global South and Global North and the feminist, SRHR, and disability justice movements to explore how cross-movement cooperation collective advocacy strategies to dismantle ableism and promote reproductive justice. Discussions covered the invisibility of certain disability groups in SRHR frameworks, the persistence of ableist and gender-based violence, and the urgent need to advance disability-inclusive policies. The circle emphasised solidarity-building across movements and the importance of shared leadership and lived experience in driving systemic change. WGG sponsored five delegates to attend and participate GDS 2025, including women with disabilities leaders. They represent organisations such as the Kenyan Network of Women with Disabilities, Women with Disabilities Development Foundation Bangladesh, Women Spaces Africa, alongside CREA and IWRAW AP representatives. They engaged in advocacy and amplified the voices of their communities on global platforms.
